captureMode: Repeated still screenshots, semantic DOM observations, responsive bounds, and a bounded in-page frame-delta smoke sample; no target-hardware performance claim.

checks.claim: The entry screen visibly presents all four requested characters, four vehicle identities, fairness rules, and an unambiguous start control.
checks.baseline: Generated neon key art, MIRRORSHIFT identity, four roster cards, equal-spec labels, catch-up and guard rules visible.
checks.action: None; entry observation.
checks.observed: Mike, Axiom/Mir, Codex, and Mirror each had a distinct labelled card and vehicle; ARM THE CIRCUIT was exposed as one accessible button.

checks.claim: Start enters a visible countdown and settles into a stable active four-racer circuit rather than false-finishing.
checks.baseline: Lobby/results screen with an enabled start or replay control.
checks.action: Clicked ARM THE CIRCUIT, then later RUN IT BACK.
checks.expected: Visible 3 countdown, then race HUD and moving racers; still racing at ten seconds.
checks.observed: Replay visibly showed 3 / GUARDS ARMED. The corrected simulation was racing at four and ten seconds with item pickups, attack events, four racers, lap 1/3, standings, catch-up, and guard HUD visible.
checks.namedSeam: A first observation exposed false lap wraps; the nearest-track search origin was fixed and a ten-second regression was added before this passing repeat.

checks.expected: Server event records the mine drop and the track shows combat activity.
checks.observed: Event feed recorded 'Mike dropped a Glitch Mine'; a mine was visible on the circuit. Player one immediately acquired another mine from a reactivated nearby pad, so the slot remained filled.

checks.claim: The shortest complete journey reaches a legible result and can begin a rematch.

checks.expected: Winner, full ranking, rule summary, and a fresh countdown.
checks.observed: CODEX WINS, all four ranked vehicles, 100% equal stats / 85% attack drops / 3 starting guards, then a fresh visible countdown. RESET returned the preview to lobby.

checks.claim: The dedicated phone controller fits a portrait phone viewport without clipping or scrolling.

checks.observed: All six interactive controls had bounds inside 390x844; scroll width and height exactly matched the viewport. The new DRIFT READY status was visible without changing the fit. Physical-device and mixed-router QA remain pending.

checks.claim: The equal-spec drift contract has visible charge and release states during a live authoritative race.

checks.expected: Segmented charge, named tier, kart sparks/slip, then a short release boost state.
checks.observed: The HUD showed 25% charge and BLUE while Mike visibly drifted; a later DOM sample caught SHIFT BOOST and the live track showed stronger exhaust/speed language. Deterministic tests separately verify tier duration and power.

checks.claim: Incoming combat warnings are visible during play rather than hidden above the viewport.
checks.baseline: A first pass exposed that lobby button focus left the page scrolled, placing the warning above the viewport.
checks.action: Reset start scroll position, raised HUD stacking, strengthened warning contrast, then repeated until a nearby mine warning fired.
checks.expected: Page remains at scroll Y 0 and a high-contrast warning appears inside the circuit frame.
checks.observed: Scroll Y was 0; MINE NEARBY became active at y=68.8 with approximately 0.96 transition opacity and was visible at the top center of the captured frame.
checks.namedSeam: Live testing found and corrected the off-viewport warning before this passing repeat.

checks.claim: The current client renderer meets a production 16.7 ms frame budget.
checks.baseline: Versioned Canvas 2D bundle in the in-app preview browser.
checks.action: Collected the most recent 180 requestAnimationFrame deltas during an active four-racer race.
checks.expected: Representative hardware profiling at or under the eventual production budget.
checks.observed: This preview sampled 42.51 ms average and 55.6 ms p95. The browser environment may schedule frames differently from target hardware, but this result cannot support a production-performance claim.

checks.claim: Mirror Core is an explicit, understandable lobby choice and cannot be confused with Circuit Crown race mode.

checks.action: Clicked the uniquely named MIRROR CORE mode button once.

checks.claim: Mirror Core active play visibly communicates a distinct arena, score race, timer, guard combat, item pressure, and all four players.

A later frame showed scores 3/3/1/0 while the event feed named a +1 guard-break score and player one had lost one guard segment.

checks.claim: Track and mode selection produce distinct adaptive score profiles rather than one renamed loop.

checks.expected: Representative listeners approve composition, engine/event balance, clipping, and fatigue on target speakers.
checks.observed: Unobserved. Functional telemetry cannot prove perceived musical or mix quality.

checks.claim: Reloading the phone controller resumes the same seat without stale-sequence input rejection.
checks.viewport: desktop browser controller surface; prior 390x844 fit receipt remains separate
checks.baseline: Seat 1 displayed MIKE, MAKER GT, LOBBY, three guard segments, and SEAT 1 // LIVE · 3MS while the server reported one active session and zero rejected actions.

checks.expected: The same session identity handshakes as resumed, advances its next client sequence, keeps Mike on seat 1, and continues receiving acknowledgements without rejection.
checks.observed: The settled controller displayed SEAT 1 // LIVE · 4MS with Mike and all controls intact. The same session id reported 2 handshakes, 1 resume, 315 accepted actions, 0 rejected actions, and next sequence 316.

checks.claim: An already-open controller visibly recovers when the authoritative server process is replaced.
checks.route: live controller plus replaced runtime on 127.0.0.1:8805
checks.viewport: same controller tab across the interruption
checks.baseline: Seat 1 controller was live with acknowledged round-trip timing.
checks.action: Stopped the exact Node process owning port 8805, observed the interruption, then started a fresh v0.7 runtime on the same port without reloading the controller.
checks.expected: The controller visibly enters a retry state, automatically handshakes again, retains p1/Mike identity, and sends a high continuing client sequence accepted by the fresh authority.
checks.observed: The middle semantic frame displayed RECONNECTING… while retaining Mike and the full controls. The settled frame returned to SEAT 1 // LIVE · 3MS. Fresh-server telemetry tied the same client session id to 102 accepted actions, 0 rejected actions, next sequence 534, and 5.2 ms p95 client-reported request-to-ack time.
checks.namedSeam: Seat identity and input recover, but replacing the authoritative process intentionally resets the in-progress match to the lobby; durable match-state persistence is not claimed.

checks.claim: Shared-screen and phone clients for one seat coexist without evicting each other's transport session.
checks.route: shared-screen and p1 controller tabs plus /api/telemetry
checks.viewport: simultaneous desktop game and controller surfaces
checks.baseline: The final v0.7 runtime started in the default Mirror Forge Circuit Crown lobby.
checks.action: Loaded both clients, waited across multiple one-second heartbeat intervals, then observed each surface and the tied server transport state.
checks.expected: Both surfaces remain live, two independent p1 session ids remain connected, and acknowledgement receipts show no session eviction or sequence collision.
checks.observed: Controller displayed SEAT 1 // LIVE · 4MS and the shared screen displayed WORKSHOP LINK // LIVE. Server telemetry reported 2 sessions, 2 active sessions, 125 accepted/applied actions, 0 rejected or ignored actions, and 5.3 ms p95 client-reported round trip. Focused HTTP evidence separately verifies that a non-owning client's neutral drive is acknowledged but ignored during the 900 ms meaningful-input lease.

checks.claim: The v0.8 lobby draft keeps four unique identities while an occupied shared-screen pick swaps ownership and survives reload.

checks.claim: A second-seat phone can draft a character, updates the shared screen, locks after start, and preserves the pick through reset.

checks.namedSeam: This browser could not natively resize the updated controller to 390px width; the live 540x720 no-scroll result does not replace a post-change physical 390px touch/LAN check.

checks.claim: The v0.9 Mirror identity produces a readable presentation-only draft cue, countdown callout, and bounded launch flourish without changing vehicle performance.

checks.baseline: Default Mike lobby with four roster cards exposing the new signature and expression labels; expression diagnostics waited for a user gesture.
checks.action: Clicked the occupied Mirror card, observed the tied motif receipt, started once, captured the countdown, first launch frame, and a later moving frame, then repeated after strengthening the short in-world labels.
checks.expected: Mirror's complete identity moves to P1; RETURN SIGNAL schedules once after the gesture; countdown names the identity; echo-prism geometry and a bounded RETURN SIGNAL label appear during launch; diagnostics explicitly deny a performance change.
checks.observed: P1 became Mirror. The draft receipt reported prism-echo, RETURN SIGNAL, draft-lock, 1 cue, 4 scheduled notes, audio scheduled, and changesPerformance=false. Countdown displayed COUNTER ANGLE // RETURN SIGNAL. Launch receipts reported echo-prism activity and named labels for all four clustered karts; a repeated Mirror launch logged 8 expression frames without obscuring standings, item HUD, track, or guards.
checks.namedSeam: The first geometric-only cluster read too subtly; a short identity label was added and the complete launch was repeated. Repeated still frames prove bounded visible states, not high-cadence animation smoothness or perceived audio quality.

checks.claim: A natural v0.9 race result carries the actual winner's expression and functional victory motif rather than a hard-coded P1 identity.

checks.baseline: P1 was Mirror while Codex remained an AI-controlled rival with the live-compile expression contract.
checks.action: Allowed the same unforced server race to resolve, then captured the settled results card and DOM-tied expression receipt.
checks.expected: Whichever racer wins supplies the result color, expression label, quote, vehicle, and victory-refrain motif metadata.
checks.observed: The natural result was CODEX WINS with ROUTE COMPILED // “ROUTE COMPILED. KEEP UP.”, Prompt Runner, Mirror Forge, and all four ranked rows. The tied receipt changed to live-compile, ROUTE COMPILED, victory-refrain, 3 cues, and 12 scheduled notes. No console warnings or errors were present.
checks.namedSeam: Scheduler state proves distinct notes were scheduled under the runtime's audio path; it does not prove that humans like the motif or that the final speaker mix is balanced.

checks.claim: The v0.9 expression renderer meets the production 16.7 ms frame budget on target hardware.
checks.route: shared screen development diagnostics after draft, launch, active race, and result
checks.baseline: Four bounded flourishes, labels, and motif diagnostics enabled; no target hardware profiler attached.

checks.expected: A representative target device sustains the declared production frame budget for a full hardware-duration session.
checks.observed: The preview sampled 24.22 ms average and 27.9 ms p95 with a 47.08% over-25-ms rate. This is better than the earlier preview smoke but remains above 16.7 ms and cannot establish causality or target-hardware performance.

checks.claim: The v0.10 race-variant selector and complete lobby fit a 1280x720 game-night display without scrolling or hiding the launch action.

checks.observed: The corrected frame showed every required lobby element and the full ARM THE CIRCUIT button with no page scrollbar. Track and signal selections updated the mode pill and dynamic lap copy.
checks.namedSeam: Live observation rejected the first valid layout because the main start action was partially clipped at the declared desktop height.

checks.claim: Shardline Sprint is a materially distinct two-lap risk format and not renamed baseline copy.

checks.expected: Every authority/HUD surface reports two laps; the world uses readable shard/risk-route language; music names SPRINT; diagnostics deny stat or catch-up changes.
checks.observed: The lobby and HUD reported SHARDLINE SPRINT // 2 LAPS and LAP 1 / 2; diagonal shard atmosphere and RISK ROUTES labeling were visible; music reported FORGE · SPRINT; 1015 visual frames accrued while changesVehicleStats and changesCatchup both remained false.
checks.namedSeam: The first live countdown exposed a visual 4 and the mode card retained stale three-lap copy. Display clamping and dynamic format copy were corrected before Redline verification.

checks.claim: Redline Gauntlet completes a natural four-lap authoritative journey with stronger presentation pressure and equal-spec results.

The natural result was CODEX WINS on NULL FOUNDRY · REDLINE GAUNTLET · 4 LAPS, with 100% equal base stats, 85% attack drops, three starting guards, and FOUNDRY · REDLINE · DEBRIEF music. checks.claim: The phone controller reflects the active race variant and dynamic lap total without removing controls or defence state.

checks.claim: The v0.10 variant renderer meets the production 16.7 ms frame budget on target hardware.
checks.route: complete Null Foundry Redline journey with DOM-tied frame diagnostics
checks.baseline: Redline atmosphere, four character expressions, HUD, adaptive score, and result presentation enabled; no target-hardware profiler attached.

checks.observed: The preview sampled 19.65 ms average and 27.8 ms p95 with a 10.42% over-25-ms rate. This improves on the v0.9 preview sample but remains above 16.7 ms and cannot prove target-hardware performance.

checks.claim: v0.11 presentation-only pose interpolation preserves the complete authored Redline and Mirror Core compositions while operating between authority packets.
checks.route: fresh v0.11 authority; Null Foundry Redline plus active Mirror Core
checks.baseline: The v0.10 client drew each server pose directly; measured authority packet cadence was approximately 90 ms.
checks.action: Selected Null Foundry and Redline through the real lobby, started active play, then independently reset into Mirror Core; collected DOM-tied interpolation/render receipts and complete screenshots.
checks.expected: Interpolation frames accrue only during active play; pose corrections remain bounded; track/arena, four racers, items, hazards, HUD, guards, standings, threats, and music identity stay visible; authoritative state and stats remain unchanged.
checks.observed: Fresh Redline accrued 74 interpolation frames with zero pose snaps while preserving the full Foundry pressure scene, four-lap HUD, attack slot, guards, standings, hazards, and music status. An earlier longer Redline sample accrued 111 interpolation frames. Isolated Mirror Core accrued 224 interpolation frames with zero pose snaps while preserving arena geometry, all four racers, score/timer, attack warnings, guards, items, and CORE DANGER music. The held-out deterministic soak separately covered 45,504 interpolated poses and 864 forced teleport snaps without packet mutation.
checks.namedSeam: Repeated screenshots and semantic receipts prove preserved composition and active interpolation state, but this browser exposes no ephemeral rolling buffer; perceived high-cadence smoothness remains UNKNOWN pending target-display observation.

checks.claim: v0.11 meets the local render-work budget and therefore already proves end-to-end 60 fps on target hardware.
checks.route: DOM-tied axm.render-performance-diagnostics/v1 under active Redline and Mirror Core
checks.baseline: The prior frame-delta-only receipt could not distinguish drawing cost from browser scheduling delay.
checks.action: Instrumented bounded Canvas stage duration, HUD update duration, authority packet cadence, interpolation activity, frame cadence, and inferred scheduling wait; repeated named race and battle workloads.
checks.expected: Local render and HUD work stay well below their budgets while any remaining end-to-end frame delay is kept separate from target-hardware claims.
checks.observed: Active Redline measured 1.44 ms average / 3.3 ms p95 render work and 0.55 / 0.8 ms HUD work. Active Mirror Core measured 1.41 / 2.8 ms render work. Preview frame p95 still ranged 34.9–55.6 ms, with 28.5–43.7 ms outside measured render work and schedulerLimited=true. The evidence proves local render-work headroom, not target-device 60 fps.
checks.namedSeam: Render execution and frame scheduling are different claims. The preview's scheduler-limited cadence cannot be promoted into either a render regression or a representative-hardware pass.

checks.claim: The V12 target-session recorder is an opt-in, legible measurement surface that can remain open or closed during active racing without changing the authored game composition.
checks.baseline: Normal game-night launch does not expose the recorder. The explicit perf query revealed TARGET LAB and opened its session panel over the complete lobby.
checks.action: Auto-started bounded smoke sessions, closed the panel, launched and observed a real Clear Signal race, reopened the panel during combat, and allowed the smoke to settle.
checks.expected: The panel states the evidence boundary, shows live measurements and zero authority writes, remains keyboard-accessible, can close without stopping the session, preserves the full racing surface when closed, and produces an export-ready receipt when settled.
checks.observed: The panel fit at 1280x720 with readable boundary, metrics, duration, controls, and privacy copy. Closing it restored the complete race view with standings, four racers, track, guards, item slot, events, music, and connection state. Reopening during live attacks showed measurement progress without gameplay or console errors.
checks.namedSeam: The recorder is a local measurement hand. Its overlay intentionally occupies part of the opt-in evidence view and is not present during ordinary game-night launch.

checks.claim: A short V12 recorder smoke cannot be mistaken for the 30-minute target-hardware gate.
checks.route: 15-second active Clear Signal smoke using axm.target-session-performance/v1
checks.baseline: The first live 12-second build correctly completed its requested duration but used generic COMPLETE wording and left the visible selector on 30 minutes, creating an admission-language ambiguity.
checks.action: Added explicit duration class and thirty-minute eligibility, corrected the live status and query-duration label, reloaded, completed a 15-second active-race smoke, and read the DOM-tied receipt seam.
checks.expected: The visible selector names the requested smoke; the result says it does not close the 30-minute gate; the receipt remains compact/private/read-only and captures active workloads.
checks.observed: The final panel displayed 15 SECOND BOUNDED SMOKE and SMOKE COMPLETE // DOES NOT CLOSE 30-MINUTE GATE. The receipt reported 15,008.7 ms, four workload segments, 221 interpolation frames, zero snaps, 49 ms preview frame p95, 1.8 ms render p95, 0.05 ms server-tick p95, one long task, false 30-minute eligibility, zero authority writes, and false retention for raw frames, user agent, and network addresses. Browser logs were empty.
